## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Water on Earth

GRACE Follow-On uses two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they approach a larger concentration of mass, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite.

The satellites’ changing separation is measured and used to infer shifts in mass. Those inferred shifts help scientists investigate changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level attributable to water added to the oceans.
